rv.q: The masterful strokes of playwright Dominque Morisseau, the visionary leadership of director Raymond O. Caldwell, and a brilliant tour de force cast make Confederates a crowning achievement at the Fountain Theatre.
Morisseau brings the two stories together without pretending that 164 years have erased the differences between them.

What comes across instead is a reductive melodrama, with mugging from the performers in place of a skilled delineation of their characters’ truths — as essential in farce as it is in kitchen sink drama.
Confederates features a fantastic cast and memorable performances.
Morisseau, the Tony Award-nominated playwright and MacArthur fellow, has constructed a remarkably inventive theatrical experience.
CONFEDERATES manages to inject humor and laughter into this very serious subject.

cn.t: Morisseau's dual-timeline drama about two Black women 150 years apart earns mostly strong notices for its powerful performances and timely themes, though some find the parallel structure uneven.
